newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index players await jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index players await jobs data.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. stock index options remained subdued Thursday ahead of Friday's May U.S. employment report and volatilities continued to edge higher, traders said.
"There's not much going on," one broker in S&P 100 index options said.
By about 1220 CDT/1720 GMT, the busiest OEX option was the June 820 put, which had traded just 3,645 contracts.
The June 830 call was behind it with turnover of about 2,070 contracts.
Among other indices, the S&P 500 was ahead 6.65 at 846.76 and the Dow industrials were up nearly 61 ponits at 7,330.
Before the stock market opens Friday, May U.S. employment data are scheduled for release. Economists on average expect an increase in payrolls of 219,000, compared with a rise of 142,000 in April.
Average hourly earnings are forecast to rise 0.4 percent after a 0.1 percent decline in April.
"At the present time, there's not much action to speak of," one S&P 500 futures options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "Everyone's probably waiting until tomorrow."
He said that although the market has been trapped in a trading range, volatilities have been creeping up in anticipation of Friday's jobless number.
Volatility on June S&P 500 futures options was up to the 19.4 to 19.5 region, up about a point from Wednesday, he said.
Volatility in OEX options, as measured by the volatility index, was up 0.47, or about 2.05 percent, at 23.19.
The VIX is calculated off certain near-month OEX options.
The CME trader said volatility in July options was also moving higher as investors, remembering the sharp market correction last July, grow fearful of a repeat.
